questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore Italy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: All the assistance I needed. They were very helpful, and quick to respond on email. However I found it a bit hard to figure out when the semester started (15th September). Luckily I had arrived one week before.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Easy, but very expensive!
I lived in a rental from Joivy. Lot of good opportunities, but also way too expensive. I don't think I would recommend Joivy. You kind of got the feeling, that they tried to get all the money out from you, as they could. And you had very bad rights as a tenant. For example they provide their right to lock themselves into the apartment and your room, even when you're not home.
But I had the impression, that all Danish people paid over 7000 DKK a month, no matter where they found their private accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it comes with a price, but then again - you're in the city center. All of the campuses is out beyond the city ring. And to me, it meant a lot to live in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy, and way more casual than at UCPH. You could switch courses through the whole semester, if you weren't satisfied or if the exam date did not match your preference.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just signed up at the UNIMI portal, very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think you could just write to the study administration. How ever, help wasn't nessecary for me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the first week to try different courses out, and then register.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNIMI offers interesting courses, however the teaching is way better at UCPH in my opinion. Especially they have a lot of interesting courses on migration studies.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Way below the UCPH level. A lot of things that you learn on year 1 or 2 at Political Science was repeated on MA-courses on UNIMI. The exams were graded very generously.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. I had one amazing teacher at "Political Order, Violence and Institutions". However also very "italian" teachers, who didn't manage to make the syllabus interesting.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Political Order, Violence and Institutions", "Geopolitics of Migrations", "Globalization, Social Justice and Human Rights", and "Conflicts, Political Arrangements, and Legitimacy"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Political Order, Violence and Institutions" - because the teacher is really great! "Geopolitics" was great in the first part.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: By living with Joivy you had to purchase all bedding, sheets and so on yourself. Other than that, none.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries was more expensive, than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not really something that was made visible for the exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know. Besides from the Erasmus-network.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Aperativo! Walking around the city. Enjoying the restaurants and cafes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I visited Bergamo, Como, and Turin on weekends, which are only a short travel from Milan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Italians are very kind and helpful!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just approach them, they are really outgoing and easy to talk to. Some approached me. How ever I dint really get any Italian friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italians tend to have a high temper:) And there is a loooot of traffic in Milan, which I personally got tired of. It was hard to find calm (and green) spaces in Milan.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the people and aperativo!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress, you will figure everything out everything out on the way! Especially if you're a master student and have electives, it is really easy to find courses. 
Try to look other Danish students to live with. A lot of Danish people lived together, I didn't, and I sometimes missed that. 
Otherwise try to reach out to someone before the exchange, so you have a "safe" person in the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to enjoy my own company, and figure out how much bureaucratic and practical burdens I can manage. And trying to be in a foreign environment in general.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Sometimes I felt lonely, and sometimes I was socially overstimulated. Both things was challenging, but also very giving. 
And all the practical stuff before arrival.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No:)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
